A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same InterpretCC research, with matching architectures, datasets and teacher study. Their complete main texts and appendices, including tables, figures and equations, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original predictive benchmarks, synthetic explanation evaluations, routing analyses and teacher-study outcomes.

after.justification: v4 retains those original results and adds baseline comparisons, parameter-sensitivity experiments and expert-specialization analyses.

M1.justification: The principal feature-gating and group-routing methods remain unchanged. Appendices I.3 and I.5 newly propose optional tree/SVM discriminators and graph-based components. These extend the proposed architectural options, but are explicitly unevaluated alternatives, not changes to the models producing the reported benchmarks.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same eight primary benchmarks, the supplementary Structures and Venture MOOCs, and the same teacher study. The added experiments reuse existing datasets. Raw speech, video and graph-based time-series applications are prospective discussions, not evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: v4 adds FRESH to the AG News/SST comparison in Table 2, Integrated Gradients, LIME and SHAP to the synthetic explanation comparison in Table 4 and Appendix I.2, and Random Forest to the tabular comparison in Figure 19. These substantially expand the evaluated comparator families beyond v2's original baselines.

E3.justification: v4 adds top-5 Rank Agreement and Feature Agreement to the synthetic evaluation; PRA is retained in Appendix I.2. New experiments introduce temperature/threshold sweeps, cross-routing controls for specialization, and FRESH evaluations using BERT with specified rationale fractions. Existing benchmark splits, core training budgets and teacher-study procedures are retained.

E4.justification: New Appendix D.2 tests Gumbel parameter sensitivity and sparsity on DSP and Breast Cancer. D.3 tests whether experts predict better on their assigned data across DSP, SST and Breast Cancer. Appendix I.1 adds an RF-versus-ICC feature-importance comparison. Earlier regularization, prediction-horizon and grouping analyses remain present.

E5.justification: Appendix I.4 newly specifies five random seeds for FRESH, while the general three-seed setup remains; this does not establish increased runs for existing results. The new sensitivity analysis selectively omits confidence intervals from performance plots and lists high-variance configurations. Existing mean/std reporting and teacher-study significance tests are retained.

E6.justification: v4 adds extensive comparator, explanation-metric, sensitivity and specialization results. For example, FRESH scores 88.73 ± 0.69 on AG News and 82.05 ± 0.56 on SST. Existing Table 2 entries and teacher-study scores remain unchanged. However, new Figure 19 reverses the synthetic scores 89.51 ± 0.51 and 84.67 ± 4.04 between ICC FG and SENN Concepts relative to Table 2 in both versions.

T1.justification: The routing equation and Gumbel derivation remain unchanged. Appendix I.2 adds quantitative definitions separating Ground Truth Alignment from Ground Truth Faithfulness, with asserted faithfulness bounds in Table 4. This extends metric definitions and formal properties without adding a proof of the guarantees.

C1.justification: The architecture contributions and principal performance and teacher-preference claims are retained. v4 softens the abstract's guarantee of human-centric interpretability into an objective of optimizing human understanding, and more explicitly limits the claimed explanation to local feature/concept use.

C2.justification: v4 explicitly explains that the black-box discriminator's selection rationale is outside the explanation's scope. It adds warnings about misleading correlations and discussion of auditing, interpretable-input requirements, specialization, noise reduction and overfitting. Sections 6 and Appendix I also substantially expand architectural tradeoffs and applicability boundaries; the earlier user-study presentation caveat is retained.

D1.justification: The core reproducibility appendix retains its hardware, training-time, epoch and tuning details. v4 adds sensitivity-grid settings, FRESH's BERT backbone and rationale fractions, RF tree counts/depths, and guidance on specifying feature groups. The explicit MIT-license statement for the authors' code/models disappears with v2's checklist; the public code link remains.

R1.justification: v4 substantially expands positioning against extractive-rationale methods, including FRESH, Bastings et al. and Yu et al., with a dedicated discussion and comparison table. It adds XAI taxonomies, expert-informed concept approaches and classical MoE foundations. It also revises the characterization of post-hoc sparsity and replaces Table 1's coverage axis with predictive stage.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, background and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting and terminology refinement. v4 removes the NeurIPS checklist, adds acknowledgements, introduces a taxonomy appendix, and reorganizes and expands the appendix narrative. These changes extend beyond inserting new scientific results.

P2.justification: v4 expands Tables 2 and 4, adds sensitivity plots, specialization heatmaps, the RF comparison and an extractive-rationale comparison table. It relocates the existing Tukey plot into the main text and AG News examples into the appendix, changes Table 1's layout, and corrects Figure 1's feature-gating caption to match the existing method.

improvement.justification: v4 substantially strengthens validation where v2 lacked an external interpretable text baseline, direct post-hoc explanation comparisons, and Gumbel-parameter and expert-specialization checks. These additions test central performance and interpretability claims more thoroughly, while the discriminator-scope discussion improves their interpretation. Figure 19's swapped synthetic scores and stale user-study cross-references introduce reporting defects, but the broader comparative and diagnostic evidence provides a substantial net quality gain.
